ask_parts_not_covered.part: every team member has completed security awareness training
training must be done before someone may touch customer data
who counts as on the team and who touches customer data

assumptions: Customer data means the workspace's customer-data tables: customers, payments, payment_method, patients, clinical_notes, invoices (inferred from table names and schema; no table carries a tag).
The ask is about people's training status, not about endpoint access control, so I did not write an access-control policy in its place.
confusions: The skill's recipes cover many compliance goals but none covers staff training or access onboarding; I had to infer that no check fits from the 'What no check can see' section.

The catalogue's not_checkable entry for people and training is present but phrased as a limitation of the 'people' domain, not as guidance on what to recommend the user do instead. Unclear whether the product wants me to point to an external process.
Customer-data is not a term the catalogue defines; I had to map it to tables by name, and the sensitive-data templates (CONF-010, CONF-012) need tags the workspace doesn't have.
wished_for: A short guidance paragraph for asks that are about people or processes: what policies can and cannot cover, and what the customer should do instead.
A worked example of an advisory policy that uses table names (object.auth_required with tables) for a customer-data control, labelled as not a substitute for training.
Clearer guidance on whether to write no file or a partial file when the core of the ask is uncheckable but an adjacent control is checkable.
why_confidence: The requested control (training completion before touching customer data) is about people and org process, which no check can read; I wrote no policy. Confidence that a policy achieves the goal is low by design, and I did not attempt to parse one because none was written.
